title: Fire & Blood
notes: Chronicle-style history; contains expanded versions of The Rogue Prince and The Princess and the Queen.

in_universe.label: 2 BC – 136 AC
in_universe.note: Wikipedia: "covers the history of Westeros from Aegon's Conquest up to and through the regency of the boy king Aegon III Targaryen"; the Conquest war is 2–1 BC and the regency ends in 136 AC (A Wiki of Ice and Fire).

title: The Rise of the Dragon
notes: Illustrated companion "written in a more encyclopedic style"; not a narrative work, so tier adjacent.

in_universe.label: 2 BC – c. 131 AC
in_universe.note: "describing the history of House Targaryen from Aegon Targaryen's conquest of Westeros to the Dance of the Dragons civil war".

in_universe.label: 37–48 AC
in_universe.note: Wikipedia: "centers on the death of Aegon I … concludes with the death of Maegor"; A Wiki of Ice and Fire: "37 AC was the final year of Aegon the Conqueror's reign" and "In 48 AC Maegor the Cruel's reign crumbled".

release.note: First published in the anthology The Book of Swords.

in_universe.label: 103–129 AC
in_universe.note: A Wiki of Ice and Fire: "The story takes off in 103 AC with the death of King Jaehaerys I … and ends in 129 AC".

release.note: First published in the anthology Rogues.

in_universe.label: 129–131 AC
in_universe.note: A Wiki of Ice and Fire: "The story begins on the third day of the third month of 129 AC"; the Dance lasts "almost two and a half years".

release.note: First published in the anthology Dangerous Women.

in_universe.label: 209 AC
in_universe.note: A Wiki of Ice and Fire: "The story takes place in 209 AC"; Wikipedia: "some 90 years before the events of the novels".

release.note: First published in the anthology Legends (ed. Silverberg). Publisher from A Wiki of Ice and Fire. Collected in A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms (2015).

in_universe.label: 211 AC
in_universe.note: A Wiki of Ice and Fire: "a year and a half after the events of The Hedge Knight"; the Timeline places it in 211 AC.

release.note: First published in the anthology Legends II.

in_universe.label: 212 AC
in_universe.note: Its A Wiki of Ice and Fire page: "It is the year 212 AC"; the same wiki's Timeline puts it in the 211 AC row.

release.note: First published in the anthology Warriors.

title: The World of Ice & Fire
notes: In-world encyclopedia narrated by a maester; not a narrative work, so tier adjacent.

in_universe.label: Dawn Age to just before the novels
in_universe.note: "details the fictional history of the Seven Kingdoms, from the pre-historic Dawn Age up to just before the main book series".

in_universe.label: 297–299 AC
in_universe.note: A Wiki of Ice and Fire: "The Prologue of A Game of Thrones takes place in 297 AC"; "Nearly all chapters … take place during 298 AC"; the final chapters are in 299 AC.

release.note: First publication (Bantam Spectra US; Voyager UK). Wikipedia's text says only "August 1996".

in_universe.label: 299 AC
in_universe.note: A Wiki of Ice and Fire: "all chapters from A Clash of Kings … take place during 299 AC".

release.note: First publication (Voyager UK); Bantam Spectra US 1999-02-02.

in_universe.label: 299–300 AC
in_universe.note: A Wiki of Ice and Fire: "most chapters of A Storm of Swords … 299 AC"; "The final chapters … take place in 300 AC".

release.note: First publication (Voyager UK); Bantam Spectra US November 2000.

in_universe.label: 299–300 AC
in_universe.note: A Wiki of Ice and Fire: "some chapters from A Feast for Crows take place during 299 AC"; "most of the chapters … 300 AC".

release.note: First publication October 2005 (UK, Voyager); November 2005 (US). Exact days appear only in a hidden wikitext comment, so they are not used.

in_universe.label: 300 AC
in_universe.note: A Wiki of Ice and Fire: "all chapters of A Dance with Dragons take place in 300 AC".

release.note: First publication (US and UK same day).

title: The Winds of Winter
notes: "the planned sixth and penultimate novel … in the works since 2011"; publication date TBD.

in_universe.label: Not yet placed (unreleased)
in_universe.note: Unpublished; no placement.

in_universe.label: Not yet placed (unreleased)
in_universe.note: Unpublished; no placement.

in_universe.label: 101–129 AC
in_universe.note: Episode 1 opens with "old King Jaehaerys I Targaryen convenes a Great Council" (A Wiki of Ice and Fire: "The Great Council of 101 AC"); episode 10 opens on Viserys's death (129 AC). Wikipedia never prints the years.

in_universe.label: 129–131 AC
in_universe.note: "covers the events of the book Fire & Blood"; the Dance of the Dragons is 129–131 AC (A Wiki of Ice and Fire).

in_universe.label: 129–131 AC
in_universe.note: "the war known as the 'Dance of Dragons' … continues".

in_universe.label: Not yet placed (unreleased)
in_universe.note: "A fourth and final season is in development and expected to be released in 2028".

title: A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms

in_universe.label: 209 AC
in_universe.note: "taking place 90 years before A Song of Ice and Fire", with "the first season covering the events of The Hedge Knight" (209 AC per A Wiki of Ice and Fire).

in_universe.label: Not yet placed (unreleased)
in_universe.note: "renewed for a second season, which will be based on The Sworn Sword and is expected to be released in 2027".

in_universe.label: c. 298 AC
in_universe.note: "The series is based on A Game of Thrones" (mostly 298 AC in the books). The show gives no year.

in_universe.label: c. 299 AC
in_universe.note: "The season mostly covers the events of A Clash of Kings" (299 AC in the books).

in_universe.label: c. 299 AC
in_universe.note: "based roughly on the first half of A Storm of Swords" (299 AC in the books).

in_universe.label: c. 299–300 AC
in_universe.note: "adapted primarily from the second half of A Storm of Swords, along with elements of A Feast for Crows and A Dance with Dragons".

in_universe.label: After season 4
in_universe.note: "takes loose inspiration from A Feast for Crows and A Dance with Dragons … also contains original content"; no year.

in_universe.label: After season 5
in_universe.note: "Much of the season's storyline is derived from content not yet published"; no year.

in_universe.label: After season 6
in_universe.note: "largely consisted of original content"; no year.

in_universe.label: After season 7
in_universe.note: "largely consists of original content … incorporating material that Martin has revealed"; no year.
